analysis.title: AI capex boom supports US large-cap value stocks
key_insights: Robeco BP US Large Cap Equities strategy owns four of the Magnificent Seven (Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon) and does not own Apple, Tesla or Alphabet.
After a weak July for tech names, some Magnificent Seven stocks now fit the strategy's 'Three Circles' screen: fair value, excellent fundamentals, good business momentum.

PM David Cohen says Nvidia trades at 15.5 times earnings, roughly the large-cap median, while earnings grow over 200% a year. He attributes the discount to market doubt about how long the profit cycle lasts.
Cohen says AI spending is above 3% of GDP, against a 1.5% peak for the railroad buildout, and calls it the largest capex cycle in US history.

The capex cycle extends beyond semiconductors to data centers, power infrastructure (transmission lines, substations), civil works, renewable energy and healthcare. Demand for copper, steel, cement and energy follows.
Cohen cites the Russell 1000 Growth Index up 7% this year against 21% for the Value Index, and describes a rotation from growth to value driven by value cyclicals with accelerating demand.
Reshoring of critical minerals, pharmaceuticals and semiconductor fabrication is described as a decade-plus investment regime.
Cohen says Meta's AI consumer agent product Muse passed five million downloads in three weeks, against 2.3 million for ChatGPT over the same period.
Cohen argues AI back-office automation favors the largest banks, which spend USD 1-2 billion a year on IT, over the roughly 4,000 US banks that are mostly regional and cannot match that spending.
Cohen concludes that scale benefits from technology shift profitability and market share to large caps, with the value side of large cap as the sweet spot.

sector_views.rationale: Large banks can fund AI automation of back-office work, while regional banks lack the IT budgets to do so.
AI and power infrastructure buildout drives demand for copper, steel, cement, machinery and energy.
Nvidia and other hyperscalers now meet valuation criteria while earnings grow quickly.

earnings_insights: Nvidia earnings growth is cited at over 200% a year by the PM, with a 15.5x earnings multiple. The report does not state whether the figures are trailing or forward.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cohen compares this with the 1.5% railroad buildout peak to argue for a long capex cycle. The report does not name a source for the figure.
Growth has lagged value this year.
Value has outperformed growth by 14 percentage points.

risk_factors: Market skepticism about the sustainability and length of Nvidia's profit cycle, which Cohen cites as the reason for its discounted multiple.
The document carries standard disclaimers that holdings are illustrative, past performance does not guarantee future results, and nothing is a buy, sell or hold recommendation.
geopolitical: Reshoring of critical mineral deposits previously dependent on China, now being developed in the US.
Reshoring of pharmaceutical and semiconductor fabrication industries.
